item.title: Traffic island causing greater traffic, congestion, road rage and reduced safety at crossing, 6th August
item.description:
Since its installation, congestion at the junction has worsened significantly. Vehicles are frequently forced to brake sharply, accelerate aggressively, and navigate the narrowed space with frustration. This has led to a daily pattern of road rage incidents, shouting, foul language, and constant horn use—noise that carries directly into our home just two doors from the junction. The increase in traffic noise and tension has created a stressful environment for residents who previously enjoyed a quieter street. More importantly, the crossing point—used regularly by school children—has become less safe. The combination of congestion, driver frustration, and obstructed visibility has made crossing more hazardous, not less. Several neighbours have raised concerns and complaints with the council, yet no meaningful response or action has been taken.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Kings Hall Road, New Beckenham, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: The traffic island at this junction is creating a dangerous and congested pinch‑point., 6th August
item.description:
Vehicles brake sharply before the narrowing and then accelerate aggressively once past it, causing continuous noise disturbance for nearby homes. Larger vehicles struggle to pass through the restriction.During peak periods (school run and evenings), queues form in both directions causing long tailbacks along Kings Hall Road and Lennard Road. The stop‑start congestion leads to persistent idling, noise, and emissions in a residential area.The current layout no longer appears suitable for present‑day traffic volumes and is creating avoidable safety risks and environmental impact. Request: Please arrange a Highways inspection and review whether the island can be redesigned or removed to improve safety and traffic flow.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Kings Hall Road, New Beckenham, Greater London
